test_title: PYST 3: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 16th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Somu has borrowed ₹10,000 from a money lender with simple interest at a rate of 7% half yearly. How much amount will he pay to the money lender after 3 years?
solution:
**Given:**

Sum = Rs. 10000, Time = 3 years 

Rate of interest = 7% half-yearly

**Formula used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

Amount = P + S.I

Here, P = Principle, T = time, R = rate

**Calculation:**

When interest is taken half yearly,

Actual rate of interest = 2 × rate of interest 

∴ R = 7 × 2 = 14%

Now, S.I = (10000 × 3 × 14)/100 = Rs. 4200

So, amount after 3 years = 10000 + 4200 = Rs. 14200

**∴ He will pay Rs. 14200 to the money lender after 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__** The rate of 7% is already given for half a year and the period is given as 3 years. So, we need to convert either rate or time to any one format.

if we take time in years then the rate per year is 7 x 2 = 14 %

if we take time in a half-year format then time = 3 x 2 = 6

Hence, the solution and answer that we have given are correct.
